{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"The footsteps stopped just outside the room. A boy appeared in the doorway, perhaps twelve years old, with a cardboard suitcase held against his chest. His hair was wet, but his coat was dry.

“Is this the right place?” he asked.

She looked at the map. The names meant nothing to her. She had spent eleven years believing the key would tell her where to go, and now a stranger was asking her for directions.

“I don’t know,” she said.

The boy nodded as though this were useful. He set down his suitcase and sat on the bench beneath the stopped clock. After a moment, she sat at the other end. Neither asked the other’s name.

Outside, the rain slowed. The tin cup rang less often, until each drop sounded separate from the last. Across the tracks, a signal lamp came on, though there were no trains due before morning.

The writer stopped there and read the passage back. The boy might have been lost. He might have been waiting for her. The lamp could mean a train was coming, or only that someone still tended the station. The writer left it glowing and sent the story to Mara.

A few minutes later, three dots appeared beneath the message, then vanished. They returned twice before Mara’s reply arrived.

“I think I would have stayed in the room too,” she wrote.

The writer looked at the sentence for a long time. Then they typed, “Until morning?”

Mara did not answer at once."}
